nodes.statement: Signed interference and model-minus-reference streams can have a nearly cancelling sum of weights. Scaling each stream to a total rate by its own sumw is invalid unless that rate and denominator describe that same stream. Preserve the generator-defined absolute integration normalization, exposure, sumw2 and covariance between correlated streams.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:signed-weights; primary references: Phys. Rev. D 110, 030001; review Kinematics, phase space and cross sections; arXiv:1405.0301, event generation and matching

obligations.description: Trace the signed weight units and integration exposure; normalize raw sums with the declared common measure and retain correlated Monte Carlo uncertainty. Never replace signed weights by their magnitudes.

nodes.statement: An on-shell colour-singlet spin-1 state cannot couple to two identical on-shell massless vector bosons, including the colour-singlet two-gluon state. Loop corrections do not evade these assumptions. Off-shell partons or additional radiation change the premises. This theorem alone does not forbid decay to massive vector bosons.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:landau-yang; primary references: Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 60 (1948) 207; Phys. Rev. 77 (1950) 242; doi:10.1103/PhysRev.77.242; Phys. Rev. Lett. 101 (2008) 091802; arXiv:0806.2864, colour-singlet and colour-octet vectors and massive final states

obligations.description: Check spin, colour, on-shell conditions and production multiplicity; justify any claimed evasion with an explicit amplitude and source.

nodes.statement: A CP-odd resonance with CP-conserving pseudoscalar production and decay vertices need not have zero interference with the gluon-fusion continuum. CP-odd production times CP-odd decay is not a single CP-odd insertion. The actual helicity amplitudes and accepted observable determine the surviving term.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:cp-odd-continuum; primary references: arXiv:1208.4018, spin-zero amplitudes and angular distributions; Phys. Lett. B 333 (1994) 126; arXiv:hep-ph/9404359, scalar and pseudoscalar interference with the gluon-fusion continuum

obligations.description: Compute the signal-continuum cross term for the supplied production and decay couplings and cuts; do not set it to zero solely from the resonance CP label.

nodes.statement: A CP-odd interference integrand cancels only under a CP-symmetric integration measure, initial-state ensemble, observable bin and acceptance. A CP-even observable alone is insufficient with asymmetric cuts. Distinguish mixing at one vertex from two CP-odd vertices in a complete amplitude.
nodes.applicability: Review this convention in the stated process, observable, phase-space domain and perturbative order; retrieval does not establish applicability.

evidence.locator: RAVEL authored convention conv:cp-even-odd; primary references: arXiv:1208.4018, spin-zero amplitudes and angular distributions

obligations.description: Check the transformation of the full amplitude and phase-space measure including cuts, beam weights and binning before dropping a cross term.

nodes.statement: There is no universal interference K-factor. Signal, background and their cross term receive different perturbative corrections. Taking the geometric mean of signal and background K-factors is an approximation that needs process and kinematic justification, not an identity.

obligations.description: Use a cited or explicitly supplied correction within its domain; carry its uncertainty for the interference term and record missing information without inventing a factor.
